scene_breakdown.flow_prompt: Professional dark studio setup, RGB lighting backdrop, macro lens shot of IDE interface Visual Studio Code running on macOS / Linux workspace.
scene_breakdown.narration: Welcome back to IDE Guide! Today we are taking an objective look at Visual Studio Code. Quick disclaimer before we start: IDE Guide is completely independent and not sponsored by any editor developer. All opinions are strictly objective.

scene_breakdown.flow_prompt: Dynamic screen recording overlay with glowing highlighted code lines in Visual Studio Code. Cinematic camera drift across developer desk with code flowing.
scene_breakdown.narration: Visual Studio Code is categorized as a Extensible General Purpose Editor. Here are the top reasons developers choose it: Massive ecosystem of over 50,000 extensions; Unrivaled language support and LSP integration; Built-in Git GUI, terminal, and debugging capabilities; Fast startup and low resource overhead compared to heavy IDEs

scene_breakdown.flow_prompt: Minimalist UI illustration showing performance meters, RAM consumption, and feature gaps highlighted in subtle amber red.
scene_breakdown.narration: However, no editor is perfect. Here are the main drawbacks you need to know: Requires heavy extension configuration for full IDE feature parity; Electron-based memory consumption can grow with heavy plugins; Telemetry collection enabled by default (can be disabled)

scene_breakdown.flow_prompt: Comparison matrix table animated on dark futuristic HUD display showing pricing tiers: 100% Free under Free / Open Source Core (MIT / Proprietary build).
scene_breakdown.narration: In terms of cost: 100% Free. Who is it best for? Web developers, Python scripts, multi-language polyglot engineers.
